title: Maintenance of Houses and Buildings 2026: Process and Costs
desc: House and building maintenance in 2026: who is responsible, whether detached houses need a procedure, inspection, repairs, records, costs under Decree 207/2026.
summary: What homeowners need to know about building maintenance: responsibility, maintenance procedures and plans, inspection, upkeep, repairs, warranty on repair work, and how maintenance costs are calculated.
body: p

A house is like a machine: with long use it needs inspection and upkeep to stay durable and safe. From 1 July 2026, building maintenance is governed by Article 65 of the Construction Law 2025, Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, and Circular 40/2026/TT-BXD on maintenance costs.
h2
1. What is maintenance, and who is responsible?
p

Maintenance means the work needed to keep a building operating normally and safely during use: inspection, monitoring, quality assessment, upkeep, repair, replacement of equipment, and so on, but it does not include changing the function or scale of the building (Clause 10, Article 2 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
p

The owner, or the person who manages or uses the building, is responsible for maintenance (Clause 2, Article 65 of the Construction Law 2025). For houses, the owner maintains the house; an apartment owner maintains their privately owned part and contributes funds to maintain the common parts (Article 130 of the Housing Law).
h2
2. Does a detached house need a maintenance procedure?
p

The maintenance procedure is prepared by the design contractor and approved by the investor before the building is put into use (Clause 2, Article 34). However, a separate maintenance procedure is not mandatory for Grade III and lower buildings, detached houses, and temporary structures, unless the law provides otherwise; the homeowner must still carry out maintenance (Clause 4, Article 34). Maintenance standards or the procedure of a similar building may be applied (Clause 5).
h2
3. What does maintenance include?
p
Under Article 36 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, the owner does the work personally or hires an organization to do it:
ul
Regular, periodic, and unscheduled inspection to detect early signs of deterioration or damage.
Upkeep according to the annual maintenance plan.
Periodic repair (replacing damaged parts and equipment) and unscheduled repair after storms, floods, impact, fire, and so on, or when deterioration affects safety.
Assessment when damage or signs of danger are found, or when a state authority requires it.
p
The annual maintenance plan includes: the name of each task, timing, method, and cost (Article 35).
h2
4. Maintenance records and warranty on repair work
ul
Keep maintenance records throughout the service life: as-built drawings, the maintenance procedure (if any), plans, inspection results, repair records, and assessments (Clause 1, Article 38).

Repair work must carry a warranty of not less than 6 months for buildings of Grade II and below and not less than 12 months for buildings of Grade I and above; the warranty retention must be not less than 5% of the contract value (Clause 5, Article 38).
If repairing or renovating a house requires a construction permit, the homeowner must apply for it; causing damage to others requires compensation (Article 135 of the Housing Law).
h2
5. How are maintenance costs calculated?
p

Maintenance costs include: upkeep costs; periodic and unscheduled repair costs; and the cost of other tasks such as inspection, monitoring, assessment, and preparing the maintenance plan (Clause 2, Article 39). Circular 40/2026/TT-BXD guides the preparation of cost estimates; the contingency is no more than 5% (Articles 3 and 4). For buildings funded from sources other than the state budget, the owner decides whether to apply this Circular (Clause 2, Article 7).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. Apartment buildings also have separate rules on maintenance funds for common areas under the Housing Law 2023 (partially no longer in force). If a house shows large cracks, tilting, or settlement, it is advisable to engage a qualified firm to assess it.
